description: Contract fixtures for PLAN 14. Each contract names the shipped schema it binds to (or states that no schema has shipped yet), the representative Go structure a fixture must decode into, and its fixtures. Edge cases list the PLAN 14 coverage and reference both the fixtures owned here and the earlier fragments under schemas/fixtures, so nothing is duplicated blindly.

contracts.note: No session input or session output schema has shipped. This fixture proposes the shape an SSH adapter and a terminal renderer could share.
PLAN 7.2 fixes tool capabilities, not names or envelopes, and no agent-tool schema has shipped. Tool names in this fixture are placeholders.
PLAN 10 requires scope, stable event ids, pagination, provenance and truncation for retrieval, but no retrieval schema has shipped. The events here are event-envelope documents, which do validate.

Intentionally not valid against configuration.schema.json version 1: that schema has no prompts group although PLAN 11 requires one. The fixture is a contract-change proposal for the main agent, which owns the shared schema baseline.

edge_cases.note: The earlier fixture is a bare result fragment; this one is a complete request/result exchange with a zero-token completion that still has a well-formed assistant message.
The earlier fixture is a session input fragment. This one carries non-ASCII text, an emoji and a combining-friendly filename through a whole exchange.
The earlier fixture is a bare content reference. These two show exact bytes travelling by reference through a model tool call and then through a committed world change set, never regenerated as text.
The earlier fixture is a single input event. These show the full path: materialization and app-candidate tool calls, then the validated artifact that is activated for the invented program.
The earlier fixture creates one directory. This one creates both missing parents in one change set and records the absence check plus directory membership revision that make the create valid.

The earlier fixture is a bare domain error. This one is the permanent research record of the denial: a typed tool error envelope with policy revision, requested path, and the fact that nothing was written.

The earlier fixture reports expected/actual revisions. These add both halves that are otherwise missing: the typed world_conflict failure and the re-staged change set the losing attempt commits after re-reading the winning version.
The earlier fixture is a bare error envelope. These show the error as a result of a real exchange, and the resulting route health transition to cooling_down with a probe schedule.

The earlier fixture is a bare error envelope. This one shows the cancelled result itself, including the partial content already streamed and the classification that the staged work was discarded rather than committed.
The earlier fixture is a bare run payload. This one is the same outcome as a persisted app.sandbox_run event envelope, and records that no state was written while the view was retained.
The earlier fixture is a retrieval-shaped fragment. These show the truncated frame stored by content reference, and a retrieval page that ends mid-turn with a usable next cursor.
